stemMd: Which principle best reflects the author's criticism of a simple argument for fees?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Time cannot be compared with money in any respect.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Only total cost matters, not who bears it.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Showing a defect in one arrangement does not by itself establish the superiority of a particular replacement.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Every alternative to a flawed system is equally good.

options.label: E
options.textMd: A service should never require payment.

explanationMd: The passage accepts that queues impose costs but denies that this alone proves fees are better. A replacement needs its own evaluation against the purpose and distribution of access.

distractorRationale.a: The hidden-price analogy is accepted as useful.
distractorRationale.b: Distribution is central to the argument.
distractorRationale.d: The passage calls for comparative evaluation.
